$comment: Power scheme GUIDs. Never hard-code one in C#.
VERIFIED 2026-07-27 against Power Setting GUIDs (WinNT.h), under GUID_POWERSCHEME_PERSONALITY:
high-performance = GUID_MIN_POWER_SAVINGS  (minimum power SAVINGS, i.e. maximum performance)
Ultimate performance is NOT in Microsoft's documented list - still unverified (N1).
O1 (closed 2026-07-27, decision 31): schemes are matched at runtime, never assumed.
matchNames - fallback match when an OEM image ships the plan under a different GUID.
English names only, so it will not help on a non-English Windows.
createFrom - template to copy when the plan is absent entirely, via the documented
createAs   - the id the copy is created under. This GUID is SYSTEVO-OWNED, not a Windows
GUID. Fixed rather than powercfg-generated so the change log can name the
scheme before it exists, and undo deletes it by id.
Only high-performance carries a template, on purpose. Ultimate Performance parks fewer cores
and is a bigger change than a tune-up should invent on a machine that never offered it - so
Gaming uses Ultimate when present, else High, else creates High. Decision 31.
